questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere with a large international community

Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, got a email with all information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find, and to find someone to ask questions

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Rooms with shared facilities

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: none i think

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If you want to socialize a lot, I think it is the best opportunity

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sometimes it can be hard to figure out what the course is about, and it is hard to get courses approved from both universities

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to apply for both approval at my host university and my own, so it was a long process

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: online seminars and fast responses through email

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very I would say, after I got all my pre-approvals I managed to registre for all courses, and therefor I didn't have to apply for further changes

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would have liked to se some evaluations of some of the courses, maybe ask around if somebody has experience with exchange

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found that some of the exams where a bit off compared to the learnings

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses where very different depend on each class

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I prefer UCPH, but maybe it is because I am used to it. I found that there was a lot of assignment, midterms and exam compared to UCPH, but then you learn how to handle that and I will take that home with me.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
New Media Challenges 
Stress and Health 
Cooperation and Competition 
Global Religion 
Ethics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
New Media Challenges 
Cooperation and Competition 

personally they where just very interesting - especially New Media Challenges, it was a hard class, but it was so interesting, and there where some great professors

questions.answer: Did do more traveling that I expected

questions.answer: Food and personal stuff - If you want to explore the country you use a lot of money. When socializing I often went out to eat a lot more than I do home

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Went to a lot of parties, and a lot of social event. Very fun, and made a lot of friends

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: As many as you can do in the beginning, if you are looking to make friends

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you are in Amsterdam, start by exploring the cites by going to cafes and parks, and it is a must to do a canaltour. Then I recommend visiting other citys as Leiden, Utrecht, Rotterdam and Haarlem. I went to Antwerpen in Belgium which is very close and a beautiful city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was okay. Somethings will be difficult, because thing will seem harder just because we are used to something else.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did not really mange to socialize with local student - only I class not privately. It would have been nice, but Amsterdam has such a large international community so you get so many international friends that did not need to socialize with locals

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mabye that the have so many test and assignments at VU compared to UCPH

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: A lot of cafes and outside seating, when it is sunny everybody is out

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Prepare for a lot of test
More self-study 
Enjoy it

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just believe in yourself it is going to be such a meaningful experience

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Speaking English everyday
knowing that you can move to anther country and you will be fine
Getting to know other people from other cultures 
Trying studying in a other placing, and gaining confidence in you academic skills

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from the people who normally support you in challenging situations or when you are sad

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I you doubting going, do it! It has been a great opportunity

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
